method: Source-of-record check at authoring time, then a separate second pass re-reading every numeric and quoted claim against the page it came from. Author and checker are the same pass, which is not the independent arrangement the older batches used.

findings.claim: Because times and rates are confounded, posterior time estimates will not approach point values even with infinite sequence data
Uncertainty partitions into branch-length sampling error, rate variation among lineages and loci, and fossil calibration uncertainty
With calibrations fixed, analysing multiple loci or site partitions is the most effective route to precision
A fossil gives a minimum age and rarely a maximum, so calibration priors encode a judgement
findings.sourceChecked: not quoted from a source read in this pass
findings.note: Standard practice, stated without attribution; the cited paper establishes that calibration uncertainty is one of the three sources, not this characterisation of it.

findings.claim: A relaxed clock produces more honest intervals rather than narrower ones
findings.sourceChecked: inference from the cited partition of uncertainty
findings.note: Our reading, written as a consequence rather than a quotation.

findings.claim: Success rates are significantly lower for recently diverged species (~75%) than for older species (~97%), P<0.00001
Fewer than 20% of described invertebrate species have sequence records in public repositories
findings.note: The figure came from a search summary of a paper we did not open. The article states that coverage is far from complete and worst for invertebrates, without a percentage.

findings.claim: Incomplete lineage sorting, continuing gene flow and insufficient accumulated substitutions explain the failure in recent divergences
findings.note: The mechanisms are standard and consistent with both sources; they are not quoted from either.

findings.claim: One hybridisation event can move a whole mitochondrial genome between species permanently
findings.note: Stated as a property of a uniparentally inherited marker, without a case or a rate.

findings.claim: eDNA surveys have a high false negative rate at low concentrations of the genetic marker
At 10 copies per litre, 97% of PCR replicates contain zero target marker copies
Sensitivity can be increased by sample volume, sample number and PCR replicates, and increasing volume yields the greatest gain
At high densities of African jewelfish 3-5 L gives >95% detection probability, while at low densities more than 100 L is needed
findings.note: The specific species and volumes came from a search summary of a paper we did not open. The article states the pattern — a few litres at high density, more than a hundred at low — without naming the species or presenting it as a quoted result.

findings.claim: Persistence is longest in solid abiotic substrates, shorter in biotic substrates, shortest in water, and degradation is fastest when warm and wet
findings.note: Stated qualitatively without figures; the ordering came from a summary rather than a page we read.

findings.claim: PCR inhibition by humic substances produces false negatives invisible without internal controls
findings.note: Inhibition is named in the source's list of false-negative causes; the humic-substance mechanism and the internal-control remedy are ours.

findings.claim: The rate of gene gain and loss is comparable to the rate of point mutations and much greater than the duplication rate
In all analysed groups of microbes, the rate of gene gain exceeds the duplication rate by at least an order of magnitude
There is considerable orderliness among thousands of trees in the microbial phylogenetic forest, and the consensus topology explains nearly 40% of the variance
The statistical tree of life represents the central current of microbial genome evolution
Core informational genes transfer rarely because they interact with many partners; metabolic and niche-specific genes transfer readily
findings.sourceChecked: not quoted from the page read in this pass
findings.note: The complexity hypothesis is standard and consistent with the review's argument; it is stated without attribution or figures.

findings.claim: High-quality draft: >90% complete, <5% contamination, encoding 23S, 16S and 5S rRNA genes and tRNAs for at least 18 of 20 amino acids
Medium-quality draft: completeness >=50% with <10% contamination; low-quality: <50% complete with <10% contamination
Finished requires a single validated contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities at Q50 or better
Completeness and contamination are estimated from single-copy marker genes, so reduced genomes are penalised and same-species contamination is invisible
findings.sourceChecked: not quoted from the page read in this pass
findings.note: The marker-gene method is named in the search summary and is standard; the two failure modes are our analysis.

findings.claim: rRNA operons are hard to assemble from short reads because they are conserved and multi-copy
findings.sourceChecked: corpus cross-reference: content/en/biology/biotechnology/bioinformatics-explained.md, already verified on repeat collapse
findings.note: Applied from an existing verified article about assembly graphs and repeats.

findings.claim: Gene gain exceeds the duplication rate by at least an order of magnitude, so a single-lineage experiment understates community-level change
Natural selection follows deductively from variation, heritability and association with reproductive success
findings.note: Carried from an existing verified article.

findings.claim: Resistance mechanisms proposed from sequence data are produced in the laboratory and found in clinical isolates
findings.note: Carried from an existing verified article rather than re-sourced.

findings.claim: Tens of thousands of generations is a great deal for a laboratory and very little for a phylum
findings.note: A framing statement with no figure attached to any specific experiment.
